title: 4 Days, 33 Years
hooks: 4 days. That's all it took to end Jensen Huang's 33 years running Nvidia.
Nvidia lost its CEO in 4 days. Would you have sold?
One email, 4 days, and a 400 billion dollar morning.

device.metaphor: Nvidia is a tower of chips that took 33 years to stack, with Jensen Huang in his black leather jacket on top; a tear-off calendar counts the four days; he takes the steps down and leaves the jacket; the tower's height is the share price; then a street of small made-up towers is Meme Street
device.opening: frame 0: the man in the black leather jacket stands arms up on the full tower while a tear-off calendar is already flipping DAY 1, 2, 3, 4, each flip a shake and a lean; on 4, inside the first second, he is thrown off the top and only the jacket lands back. Then YEARS races to 33 and locks green as the tower pulses
device.palette: chip green and leather black with silver edges on green-black, alarm red for the fall, amber tags
device.hud: left: STATUS (CEO, IN TROUBLE, OUT, UNDER FIRE, STEPS DOWN, INTERIM CEO, YOUR MOVE, MEME STREET, YOUR TURN); middle: YEARS counting to 33, later COMPANIES to 180+; right: DAYS 0 to 4, then WIPED racing to $400B+, then NEWS, then PRACTICE 1,000 MB

scenes.vo: 4 days. That's all it took to end Jensen Huang's 33 years running Nvidia.
On Sunday he admitted an affair. On Wednesday, the New York Times reported a second, with an executive who reported to him.
With the board investigating, on Thursday he stepped down as chief executive and left the board.
The stock fell more than 13% in early trading, over 400 billion dollars, then won back more than half.
No chart warned you. So what's your move on a headline like that: sell, or hold?
On Meme Street, over 180 made-up companies have bosses too, and news hits their prices the same way.
Practise the shock with 1,000 memebucks of practice money, no cash value, before it costs you real money.
